source_name: CBCG — Registri (platni promet): registers of payment-system participants and institutions
why_relevant: Registers of banks, payment institutions and e-money institutions participating in the ME payment system. Not procurement, but the authoritative actor map against which procurement winners and their bank customers are resolved; also reveals new licensed payment players who become buyers of payment infrastructure.

source_name: Posta Crne Gore — Javne nabavke
why_relevant: State-owned postal operator, a major buyer of counter/teller equipment, cash handling, POS and payment-transaction (platni promet) infrastructure and IT, and itself a retail payments and e-fiscalisation service provider. Its procurement page plus its CeJN filings show who equips the largest branch network in ME.

source_name: Drzavna revizorska institucija Crne Gore (DRI) — audit reports incl. IT-system audits
why_relevant: Supreme audit institution. Its financial and IT-system audit reports itemise spend on software licences, information-system maintenance and technical support, name systems and often suppliers, and audit the regularity of the procurements behind them — an independent cross-check on CeJN awards and a way to see multi-year vendor lock-in at state buyers (e.g. Uprava prihoda i carina, health IZIS, registers).

source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore (gov.me/mif) — contracting authority incl. Drzavni trezor
why_relevant: Owner of the state Treasury and of the public-procurement policy function; buyer of the integrated Treasury information system (SAP) and its maintenance — an observed, concretely named recurring contract. Its annual Izvjestaj o radu describes IT projects and their suppliers/status. gov.me hosts documents on the wapi.gov.me document store.

source_name: wapi.gov.me — Government of Montenegro document/download store
why_relevant: Backing file store for gov.me: procurement standard forms (STANDARDNI FORMULAR), plans, work reports, commission reports are all served from here as /download/{uuid} or /download-preview/{uuid}. Any harvesting pipeline for ME state buyers must resolve and archive these UUID links.

source_name: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore — e-fiscalisation regulation and procurement
source_subtype: tax authority / sectoral regulator + contracting authority
why_relevant: Tax and customs authority: owner of the elektronska fiskalizacija platform and the registry/certification regime for software and POS producers. It both procures the central fiscalisation system (system software upgrades, process modelling, user support — observed in its draft Pravilnik/tender material) and defines who may legally sell fiscal POS in ME. Directly determines the addressable POS/payments vendor set.

source_name: Glavni grad Podgorica and other municipal contracting authorities (smart POS / ticketing / payment kiosks)
why_relevant: Municipalities are a distinct buyer class for payment acceptance hardware outside banking: an observed live example is 'Nabavka i ugradnja smart POS terminal validatora' by Glavni grad Podgorica (transit fare validators). Also Opstina Bar and municipal utilities (Komunalne usluge Podgorica) publish award notices. Reveals non-bank POS competitors selling into ME.

source_name: Elektroprivreda Crne Gore (EPCG) — Javne nabavke
why_relevant: Largest state-owned utility and a mass-billing/collection organisation: buys IT, billing, cash-collection and payment-acceptance services at scale. Together with CEDIS (distribution) it is a bellwether state buyer for payment and IT vendors outside the banking sector proper.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — Portal javnih nabavki page
why_relevant: Chamber of Commerce signposting page for public procurement; useful pointer to procurement rules, business-side guidance and to which member companies position themselves as suppliers to the state. Snowball source for supplier names and sector associations (ICT grouping).

source_name: Institut alternativa — public procurement monitoring and analysis
why_relevant: Leading ME think tank with a multi-year public-procurement monitoring programme; publishes analyses of reporting quality, direct agreements and corruption risk. Provides methodological caveats (what CeJN under-reports, how aggregate figures are distorted) that any quantitative use of ME award data needs.

source_name: MANS — Javne nabavke category (investigative procurement monitoring)
why_relevant: Anti-corruption NGO running procurement monitoring (incl. Balkan Tender Watch). Its case write-ups often reconstruct full award chains including supplier ownership and repeat winners — supplying the who-actually-wins narrative behind CeJN records, plus FOI (slobodan pristup informacijama) techniques for documents not published on CeJN.

source_name: Zakon o javnim nabavkama Crne Gore (consolidated text) — Paragraf.me / Sluzbeni list CG
why_relevant: The consolidated Public Procurement Act (Sl. list CG 74/19, 3/23, 11/23) defines publication duties, thresholds, procedure types (otvoreni postupak, jednostavna nabavka, direktni sporazum) and the standard forms (Obrazac 1-18). Needed to know what MUST be published — and therefore what absence in CeJN actually means — and to build the document-type taxonomy for parsing.

source_name: EBRD Client eProcurement Portal (ECEPP) and World Bank procurement — Montenegro financial-infrastructure projects
why_relevant: IFI-financed procurement runs OUTSIDE CeJN, and this is where the largest ME payments-infrastructure work is landing: the World Bank approved a EUR 8m loan for the Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA-alignment (TIPS clone) project in July 2025. Tender notices and contract awards under such loans identify the vendors building ME instant payments — the single most strategically relevant public procurement stream in this cell.

source_name: MONSTAT public-procurement contract documents (example of buyer-side self-publication)
why_relevant: Demonstrates a persistent ME pattern: individual contracting authorities also self-publish award decisions (Obrazac 18 / odluka o izboru) as PDFs on their own sites, sometimes with documents that are hard to locate on CeJN. Worth a standing sweep across state-body domains for /javne nabavke/ugovori/ directories.

source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Official Journal S-series), Montenegro-filtered notices
why_relevant: Publishes in full all EU/IPA-funded contract notices, award notices and modifications where the place of performance or contracting authority is Montenegro, including EU Delegation Podgorica service contracts for financial-sector and public-finance IT. Award notices name the winning supplier/consortium and value — the single richest supranational vendor-attribution source for ME.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders / Publications Office 'EU tenders' procurement database (DG NEAR, IPA external actions)
why_relevant: Hosts procurement detail pages for EU-institution and IPA-financed contracts covering the Western Balkans, e.g. WBIF Infrastructure Project Facility TA lots including the Digital sector; discloses scope, budget and awardee for the consultancy consortia that design financial-infrastructure projects before national rollout.

source_name: EEAS — Delegation of the European Union to Montenegro: tender and contract award notices
why_relevant: The EU Delegation in Podgorica is the contracting authority for a large share of IPA service contracts in Montenegro (public finance management, public procurement reform, investment agency TA). It publishes service contract award notices with contractor name and contract value, plus cancellation notices — often the earliest public naming of the implementing consultancy.

source_name: EBRD Contract Awards Notification pages (project procurement)
why_relevant: Consolidated EBRD disclosure of awarded project contracts; complements ECEPP by giving a structured, historically archived view of who won EBRD-financed contracts in Montenegro.

source_name: EBRD corporate consultancy contract awards lists (annual PDFs)
why_relevant: Annual PDF lists of consultancy contracts awarded by EBRD itself reveal which advisory firms EBRD repeatedly uses for financial-sector assignments in the Western Balkans; useful for competitor/partner mapping even when the assignment country is aggregated.

source_name: World Bank Projects & Operations — Montenegro project pages (incl. Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA TIPS-clone project)
why_relevant: The EUR 8m Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization and SEPA Alignment Project (TIPS clone, Banca d'Italia solution) is the single most consequential donor-funded payments programme in ME. Project pages carry PAD, procurement plans, PIDs and implementation status reports naming the beneficiary (CBCG/Ministry of Finance) and the technical solution — a direct pipeline signal for payment-systems vendors.

source_name: World Bank STEP-derived Procurement Contract Awards datasets (Finances One)
why_relevant: Machine-readable register of every contract awarded under World Bank Investment Project Financing, sourced from STEP. Filterable to Montenegro borrower contracts, giving supplier name, country, method and amount — the definitive award-attribution layer for WB-funded financial-infrastructure work.

source_name: World Bank ECA regional brief — Western Balkans Payment Modernization / SEPA programme
why_relevant: Programme-level narrative that explains the EU–World Bank–RCC architecture behind Montenegro's October 2025 SEPA accession and the instant-payments roadmap; sets the sequencing of national procurements that follow.

source_name: UNDP Procurement Notices portal — Montenegro country feed (UNDP-MNE-*)
why_relevant: UNDP Montenegro procures ICT hardware and advisory services for government beneficiaries (Secretariat General, social protection sector) — adjacent to and sometimes overlapping with digital-finance/e-government delivery. Notices carry reference numbers, beneficiary institution and specification detail.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro country office procurement page + tenders archive
why_relevant: Country-office landing page pointing to the Quantum supplier portal, current solicitations and a historical tenders archive — the archive is the retrospective record for who bid/won locally.

source_name: WBIF — Western Balkans Investment Framework project and news database (Montenegro / Digital Future sector)
why_relevant: WBIF blends EU grants with IFI loans and funds the Infrastructure Project Facility TA that writes the tender documents, procurement strategies and market models later used in national procurements. Montenegro digital/broadband TA projects here name the lead IFI (e.g. EBRD for IPF 11) and grant values, giving 12–24 months of lead time.

source_name: EIB — Calls for expression of interest / technical assistance procurement (incl. WBIF IPF lots)
why_relevant: EIB publishes the IPF technical-assistance calls covering the Digital Economy sector for the Western Balkans and, separately, contract notices for projects it finances outside the EU. These identify the consultant consortia that shape Montenegrin digital/financial-infrastructure investments.

source_name: EIB press releases — Montenegro country stream
why_relevant: EIB Global announcements for Montenegro (e.g. >EUR 250m package covering SMEs, healthcare, energy; education digitalisation grants) pre-announce loan envelopes whose downstream procurements include IT and payment-adjacent equipment; useful for pipeline dating and beneficiary identification.
